title: THE WARDEN OF SEVEN STREETS
deck: A superhuman rescue diver has walled off seven streets of Port Calder to stop the stairwell fires, and a police assault is six days away. Illuminara asks permission at every corner, and carries back what the residents cannot say to him.
shape: Seven scenes across six days: a line of broken paving, a walk at dusk, a kitchen where the unsaid is spoken, a roof at dawn, a founding meeting that ends in a fire lane, a night fire at Number 9 that the watch answers without him, and a morning when the wall becomes a chair.

scenes.title: The Line at Calder Lane
paragraphs: *Haddon Rise, Calder Lane cordon · six days before the assault, 17:40*

The paving had been broken on purpose. For forty metres along Calder Lane the street stood in slabs the size of doors, tipped on edge like a row of teeth, and no van would cross it. Beyond the slabs lay Haddon Rise: seven streets, four thousand people, and a man who had said that nobody came in without his word.
Commander Ines Ruiz stood at the tape holding a mug she had stopped drinking from an hour ago. She had the look of someone who disliked her own briefing.

**Ruiz**  
Five o'clock on the twenty-third, my unit goes in through Linden Row. Warrants, a medical team, a plan I would call acceptable if he were an ordinary man. He is not. Can you stop him?

**Illuminara**  
Yes.

**Ruiz**  
Then why are you still standing on my side of the tape?

**Illuminara**  
Because on the night I stop him, the men who have been burning those stairwells get the streets back, and they will not be afraid of your unit. Who is in the stairwells that first night?
Ruiz looked at the slabs for a while.

**Ruiz**  
That is not in my warrant. Hear this too. He has put a wall round four thousand people. The next man who does it will not have been a rescue diver. Somebody has to say the wall is the crime, whatever stands behind it.
Illuminara thought that both halves were true. She went up to the last slab and stopped. The line was his, and she waited the way one waits at a door that is not one's own.

He came out of the dusk without hurrying: fifty or so, broad through the shoulders, with the pale rope-scars of a long career in cold water on both forearms. He did not stand like a man making a threat. He stood like someone who had been standing for nineteen days.

**Dov**  
You're the one they send to stop people.

**Illuminara**  
I'm the one asking to come in.

**Dov**  
You could put me on the ground. I saw you hold up that bridge on the news. Fine. Then who stops them? Show me one thing in this city that has stopped them without me. One.
She had a true answer, which was nothing, and she let him have it.

**Illuminara**  
I can't. Not yet. May I walk your streets with you tonight and not say a word about the assault?

**Dov**  
Walk. Nobody leads you, and you ask at every corner.

scenes.title: Seven Streets at Dusk
paragraphs: *Haddon Rise, Linden Row to the river steps · six days before the assault, 18:30*

She asked at every corner. May I? He said yes each time, a little stiffly, like a man who had not been asked anything for a long while by someone he was not afraid for. Behind the windows lamps came on. Curtains moved aside and fell back. When Dov passed, voices dropped, the way voices drop for a surgeon who is also a neighbour.

Number 4 had soot to the second floor. At Number 11 a laminated notice, curling at the corners, gave the name Hanne Ostrov, seventy-one. Under it, newer, was Marcus Bell, nineteen. Both had been on stairs when the smoke came.
On Linden Row a woman of about sixty-eight, reading glasses on a chain, came down her step with a tin cup and put it in Illuminara's hands.

**Perpetua**  
Evening, Warden.

She said it to the air above Dov's shoulder, in the voice one uses to a large dog one is fond of and wary of. Dov inclined his head and went on toward the next lamp. Illuminara stood holding tea from a woman who had not yet decided about her, and felt a small undeserved happiness she did not examine.
On the steps of Number 9 a girl of seven was drawing on the pavement with a stub of chalk.

**Nell**  
This is the seven streets. This is Mr Dov, he stands here at night. This is Mama's window. This is where the fire goes.

**Illuminara**  
And where do you go when it comes?

**Nell**  
Down. But there isn't a door at the bottom of our stairs any more. Somebody took it.

Dov had stopped three steps away. He looked into the stairwell, at the pale rectangle on the plaster where something had once been hung, and a muscle at the back of his jaw moved once. He did not say that he had not known.
Illuminara sat down on the step beside the chalk and asked to be shown Mama's window.

scenes.title: What They Would Not Say
paragraphs: *Perpetua Vane's kitchen, Linden Row · five days before the assault, 21:15*

Dov had gone to the river steps for the night watch. The kitchen smelled of onions and radiator dust. Two people had come, and they sat with their coats on, the way people sit who may need to say later that they were never there.

**Teodor**  
My brother's dialysis nurse hasn't come in nine days. The ambulance asks for the Warden's word at the line, and the Warden is at the other end of seven streets. Don't tell him I said so. He pulled my boy out of the river.

**Perpetua**  
Write it down in that order. We love him. Then: we have not had a visitor, a vote or a wedding in three weeks. And when the tactical comes, half of us will stand behind him because there is nowhere else to stand.

**Illuminara**  
I would like to carry that to him. Only what you let me carry.

**Teodor**  
Tell him about the nurse.
Perpetua went to the dresser and came back with a biscuit tin. Inside lay a thick fold of pink and yellow carbon paper, soft with handling.

**Perpetua**  
Nineteen years I dispatched for Marrow and Pike. Every stairwell fire on the Rise has a work order two or three days before it. Remove self-closing fire door, replace with plain. Authorised, G. Pell. I took the carbons out in this tin the day they laid me off, because I am that kind of woman. I took them to the council twice. One tenant with a tin is a complaint. They told me I had no standing.

**Illuminara**  
What gives you standing?

**Perpetua**  
A registered body. Seven signatures, one from each street, and a chair. Then the inspector has to open a file, and that is the difference between a complaint and a case. I have six streets. I do not have a street that trusts a union more than it trusts the man on the line.

Illuminara turned the carbons over. G. Pell. G. Pell. A date, a stairwell, and three days later a fire. She had come to understand a man, and she was holding a ledger, and she saw that these were the same errand.

scenes.title: The Roof of Number Four
paragraphs: *Number 4 Linden Row, roof · four days before the assault, 05:10*
Dov sat on the parapet with his boots over the street, watching the grey come up behind the river cranes. She stood three paces back until he said she could come closer.

**Illuminara**  
Some of them told me things they could not say to you. I have their leave to say them. Do you want them?

**Dov**  
Say them.

She said them in the order Perpetua had asked for. We love him. No visitors, no votes, no weddings. Half of us stand behind you because there is nowhere else. And the nurse. He listened the way he must once have listened to a gauge on the way down, without moving.

**Dov**  
Teodor said that.

**Illuminara**  
Last.

**Dov**  
I turned her back myself, on the eleventh day. I couldn't tell you why. She wore a vest.
Below, a milk float went down Linden Row. The sky had begun to separate the roofs.

**Dov**  
You want me to stand down.

**Illuminara**  
No. If you stood down tonight you'd be a man with a pension and a dead stairwell, and Pell would be back by midnight. The wall stays until something else is standing where it stands. I want to know what you are afraid of on the day you are not here.

**Dov**  
That I'm at the river steps. Hanne's door, Marcus's door, both times I was at the wrong end of the district. I'm good in water. Fire comes up a stair. One man can't be at nine stairwells.

**Illuminara**  
Nor can I.
She laid Perpetua's carbons on the parapet, photographed and flat. He read the first and then the next with a diver's patience, running his thumb along each line as along a log.

**Dov**  
Authorised, G. Pell. How many of these?

**Illuminara**  
Eleven so far. Perpetua has more. Alone they are a complaint. She needs seven streets, and one of them is yours.

**Dov**  
And they don't trust a union more than they trust me.

**Illuminara**  
Not yet. I think they might if you were in the back row.

scenes.title: Seven Signatures
paragraphs: *Linden Row hall · three days before the assault, 19:30*

Forty folding chairs, a tea urn, a card table with a pad on it. Perpetua sat behind the pad. Six streets had signed already. The river street's seat stood empty, and its likeliest steward was leaning on the back wall with his arms folded while its residents carefully did not look at him.

**Perpetua**  
Sit down, Warden. Seats are by street.

He sat. Inspector Amara Hale, who had come over the slabs that afternoon under her own fire-inspection warrant, with Illuminara's arm over the broken paving and Dov standing aside at the line rather than stopping her, waited until the chairs stopped scraping.

**Hale**  
I will say to the room what I said at the tape. I walked in today on my own authority, to look at your stairwells, and he chose not to stop me. That is all it was. I cannot open a file on a district whose gates are held by one man, and I will not rest a case on a door that one man opens for me.

**Dov**  
Then I move the line. My word at the slabs for you, the fire service and any officer with a warrant. Not the tactical.

**Perpetua**  
Your word is the problem, Warden. It is a very good word and it is one man's.

**Hale**  
Two things, and please hear them apart. Tonight, with no file and no warrant, I can post a pumper and crew inside your line under the fire code, and order a self-closing door fitted in every stairwell that is missing one. Those are hazards I can see. The case is the other thing. Carbons in a biscuit tin are a pattern, not proof. I match them to the council's log and the contractor's own invoices first, which is two days, and then a file, in seventy-two hours as a rule. If I find a man with a can, I need none of that. I take him. And Commander Ruiz goes in on the twenty-third unless I can show her something that works.

**Perpetua**  
Then we read the terms. One. The seven stewards hold the streets' access, one vote each, by hands, in this room. Two. No steward, no street and no Warden turns away a nurse, a visitor, a wedding or a fire engine. Three. The watch answers to a rota, the rota answers to this room, and any steward can be taken off by a show of hands.

**Teodor**  
You held that line twenty-two days for us and I never thanked you, so I'll ask it plain. One vote. No gate. And if we outvote you, you take it and you sit down.

**Dov**  
And the next man who comes up Calder Lane with a can?

**Perpetua**  
Meets Teodor and a rota.
Dov looked at the pad for a long time. His arms came unfolded by degrees, as if each one had to be persuaded separately.

**Dov**  
Then the lane first. Tonight, before a single stair has a watch on it. A pumper that has to wait at my slabs is not protection, it is a favour. Twenty-two days I held that gate. One vote. No gate. Yes.
Perpetua called the river street's hands and counted them twice, because nobody in the room trusted a quick count.

**Perpetua**  
Eleven to eight. The river street sends Dov Kessarin. Eight of you may tell him why, to his face, in this room, whenever you like.

The pad went round. Seven names went down, one to a street. The last was Dov Kessarin, Number 4 Linden Row, steward. He read the paper through before he signed, as he must have read every release before every dive.

**Perpetua**  
Stairwell watch. Two to a stair, a radio each, nobody alone on a landing. Teodor has Nine, and the visitor goes with him.

**Illuminara**  
My shift, no special post.

**Perpetua**  
You will hold a bucket like a stranger. Good. We'll teach you.

Outside, Perpetua had chalked the fire lane that afternoon on the presumption: three metres wide, the whole length of the slabs, in white lines like a pedestrian crossing laid by someone with a grudge. Dov stood at the first slab and looked back at the hall door, where forty people had come out to watch. He put his boot down once. The paving came apart along the chalk like ice along a pond, and stopped at the lines.

By the time the shovels came he was sitting on the kerb with his big hands between his knees. Illuminara took the first barrow. It weighed what a barrow weighs. By morning the lane was open and Hale's pumper stood inside the line with its blue light off, and the only thing in the district that could close the road again was a vote.

scenes.title: Number Nine
paragraphs: *Number 9 Calder Lane, stairwell · two nights before the assault, 02:40*
The rota had put Dov on the river steps, six hundred metres from Calder Lane. He had asked for it. It was the wrong end of the district, and he wanted to see what that cost.

At Number 9 the watch was Teodor on the ground-floor landing and Illuminara two flights up with a flask and a radio she held like a borrowed instrument. At twenty to three the smell reached her before the sound: petrol, then smoke, rolling up the open throat of the stairs where the bottom door should have been.

**Teodor**  
Nine, Nine. Man at the foot with a can. Fire's on the stair. Pumper, Nine. The Drays are on the third.

He said it in a perfectly steady voice, the voice of a night nurse. Illuminara was past the second landing before he had finished. Down the lane, in the gap that had not existed two days ago, an engine caught.

The third-floor landing was going. Flame had eaten the plain wooden door and was climbing the stringers, and the Drays, five of them and a grandmother in a kitchen chair, stood at the top of a stair that would not carry them. The slab sagged and cracked. Illuminara put her back under it. She had held a bridge once; this was lighter, and it was on fire, and she did not tell herself it was only a landing. The weight came down through her shoulders and into the wall. The family went past her in a line, the grandmother carried by the eldest boy, through a heat that smelled of her own hair.

Below, the watch did what a watch is for. Teodor put an extinguisher into the base of the fire from the doorway and handed it to a neighbour from the first floor, who took a second from the wall and stood beside him. A man in a council hi-vis who had tried to run for the lane found a bicycle lock round his ankle and Teodor on top of him. The pumper came up the lane in forty seconds, through the gap the district had voted itself, and its crew ran a line to the door.

On the river steps, six hundred metres away, a man put down his flask and listened to all of it on a handset: Teodor's voice, the pumper's, a crew chief calling clear on three. He was running before it ended.
By the time Dov came up Calder Lane the stair was black and wet and the Drays were on the pavement under a blanket.

**Dov**  
Is everyone out?

**Teodor**  
Everyone. This is Cole Rudd, Marrow and Pike, fitter. I'm sitting on him.

**Dov**  
That was without me.

**Illuminara**  
Yes.

**Teodor**  
The lane's the union's. We voted it. You were there.

**Dov**  
One thing.

He said it quietly, as one reads out a depth. Then he sat down on the kerb beside the man in the hi-vis, who looked at him with the particular fear of someone who had expected a wall and found a neighbour.

scenes.title: The Steward's Chair
paragraphs: *Calder Lane cordon · the morning of the assault, 05:00*

Hale had spent two days in the council records office with Perpetua's tin, Marrow and Pike's own invoice book and a clerk who owed her nothing. Eleven carbons matched eleven invoices, and the signature G. Pell matched the one on a payroll sheet. Rudd, held since the fire, had stopped saying he was lost.

At five she served the warrants herself, with six uniformed officers and a steward from each street walking beside them. Pell was taken at a flat in the harbour district; the dispatcher who had typed the orders was taken at a breakfast counter, a work-order book in his coat. A fire door was fitted or a fitting order posted on every stairwell on the Rise, and Marrow and Pike's contract was frozen pending audit. The owners were already hiring lawyers, Hale said dryly, and the Rise would still have its inspector.
The tactical unit did not go in. Ruiz stood at the tape with the same mug.

**Ruiz**  
The order came down at four. Uniformed warrants, escorted by your stewards. Mine stays at the cordon. I am not calling it off because the case is finished. It isn't. I am calling it off because there is nothing left for my unit to do that a fire lane, a rota and a warrant are not already doing. I want it noted that I still think a wall is a wall.

**Dov**  
It is. I was one for twenty-five days. I'll lose my licence for the paving.

**Ruiz**  
You'll be charged for the paving and censured for the rest. I'll note you broke the forty metres the vote gave you and not an inch more.

**Dov**  
Note that the watch held Number 9. I wasn't there.

Nothing that morning gave back Hanne Ostrov or Marcus Bell. Illuminara, her palms in white dressings that would be unnecessary by evening, said their names once in her head and did not offer anyone a lesson.

Dov crossed the line on foot, along the lane he had broken himself, and did not stamp. Perpetua was waiting on the far side with a tally book, and the hall behind her was filling for the first full session of the seven stewards. The dialysis nurse had come through the lane on the first morning after it opened, in her vest, and sat four hours with Teodor's brother. She was in row four now with a flask. She said nothing to Dov and he said nothing to her, and after a moment she moved her bag off the chair beside her.

**Perpetua**  
Seat by street, Steward. Row four. You're next to the nurse.

He sat. He opened the tally book to the first blank page and wrote a line in the hand of a man who had spent a career writing depths: Number 9, bottom door, fit today. Watch tonight: Teodor, Dray, Kessarin.

Outside the hall Nell was redrawing her map. The man who stood at night was gone from it. In his place she had put seven small circles, one to a street, and in the middle a larger one with a roof and a door and, in letters as tall as she was, HALL.

Illuminara sat on the kerb among the chalk dust with her ruined hands in her lap and listened to a district make a noise it had not made in twenty-five days, which was the noise of four thousand people arguing about chairs.

critic_line: Illuminara does not break Dov Kessarin's wall; she listens until the seven streets can replace it with a voted fire lane, a shared watch and a removable steward, and Dov freely chooses to sit among the people he protected.

shared_strengths: A warm superhero story that turns down violence: the problem gets solved through consent, a ledger kept in a biscuit tin, and a vote. The characters are vivid (Perpetua, Nell, Dov) and the payoffs land. The procedural meeting scene and the script-style dialogue layout may slow some readers. The quiet ending sticks, but there's no big emotional peak.

Strong emotional stakes, distinctive dialogue, and a satisfying transformation from superhuman guardianship to collective responsibility should engage these readers. Dov's vulnerability, Perpetua's authority, and the earned rescue make the central idea memorable. Procedural exposition occasionally slows momentum, and the investigation resolves conveniently quickly, but the humane ending rewards sustained attention.
shared_reservations: Two things, and please hear them apart. Tonight, with no file and no warrant, I can post a pumper and crew inside your line under the fire code
I match them to the council's log and the contractor's own invoices first, which is two days, and then a file, in seventy-two hours as a rule.

translation_sl.title: VARUH SEDMIH ULIC
translation_sl.deck: Nadčloveški reševalni potapljač je zagradil sedem ulic Port Calderja, da bi ustavil požare na stopniščih, policijski napad pa je oddaljen šest dni. Illuminara prosi za dovoljenje na vsakem vogalu in mu prinese nazaj tisto, česar mu prebivalci ne zmorejo povedati.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v šestih dneh: črta razbitega tlaka, sprehod v mraku, kuhinja, v kateri je izrečeno zamolčano, streha ob zori, ustanovni sestanek, ki se konča z gasilskim pasom, nočni požar pri Številki 9, na katerega straža odgovori brez njega, in jutro, ko zid postane stol.

scenes.title: Črta na Calder Lane
paragraphs: *Haddon Rise, zapora na Calder Lane · šest dni pred napadom, 17:40*

Tlak je bil razbit namenoma. Štirideset metrov vzdolž Calder Lane so ulico zapirali tlakovci v velikosti vrat, postavljeni pokonci kakor vrsta zob, in noben kombi jih ni mogel prečkati. Za tlakovci je ležal Haddon Rise: sedem ulic, štiri tisoč ljudi in moški, ki je rekel, da brez njegove besede nihče ne vstopi.
Poveljnica Ines Ruiz je stala ob traku in držala skodelico, iz katere je nehala piti pred eno uro. Videti je bila kot nekdo, ki mu ni všeč lastno poročilo.

**Ruiz**  
Ob petih triindvajsetega moja enota vstopi skozi Linden Row. Nalogi, medicinska ekipa, načrt, ki bi ga označila za sprejemljivega, če bi bil navaden človek. Ni. Ga lahko ustavite?

**Illuminara**  
Da.

**Ruiz**  
Zakaj potem še vedno stojite na moji strani traku?

**Illuminara**  
Ker bodo tisto noč, ko ga ustavim, možje, ki zažigajo ta stopnišča, dobili ulice nazaj, vaše enote pa se ne bodo bali. Kdo bo prvo noč na stopniščih?
Ruiz je nekaj časa gledala tlakovce.

**Ruiz**  
Tega ni v mojem nalogu. Slišite tudi to. Okoli štiri tisoč ljudi je postavil zid. Naslednji, ki bo to storil, ne bo reševalni potapljač. Nekdo mora reči, da je zid zločin, ne glede na to, kaj stoji za njim.
Illuminara je pomislila, da sta obe polovici resnični. Stopila je do zadnjega tlakovca in se ustavila. Črta je bila njegova in čakala je tako, kakor človek čaka pred vrati, ki niso njegova.

Iz mraka je prišel brez naglice: kakih petdeset let, širokih ramen, na obeh podlakteh blede brazgotine od vrvi iz dolge kariere v mrzli vodi. Ni stal kakor človek, ki grozi. Stal je kakor nekdo, ki stoji že devetnajst dni.

**Dov**  
Vi ste tista, ki jo pošljejo ustavljat ljudi.

**Illuminara**  
Jaz sem tista, ki prosi, da sme vstopiti.

**Dov**  
Lahko bi me položili na tla. Na poročilih sem videl, kako ste držali tisti most. Prav. Kdo jih potem ustavi? Pokažite mi eno stvar v tem mestu, ki jih je ustavila brez mene. Eno.
Imela je resničen odgovor, ki je bil nič, in mu ga je pustila.

**Illuminara**  
Ne morem. Ne še. Smem nocoj hoditi po vaših ulicah z vami in ne reči niti besede o napadu?

**Dov**  
Hodite. Nihče vas ne vodi in vprašate na vsakem vogalu.

scenes.title: Sedem ulic v mraku
paragraphs: *Haddon Rise, od Linden Row do rečnih stopnic · šest dni pred napadom, 18:30*

Vprašala je na vsakem vogalu. Smem? Vsakič je rekel da, nekoliko togo, kakor človek, ki ga že dolgo ni nič vprašal nekdo, za kogar ga ni bilo strah. Za okni so se prižgale svetilke. Zavese so se odmaknile in znova padle. Ko je šel Dov mimo, so glasovi utihnili, kakor utihnejo za kirurgom, ki je tudi sosed.

Številka 4 je bila ožgana do drugega nadstropja. Pri Številki 11 je plastificirano obvestilo z zavihanimi vogali nosilo ime Hanne Ostrov, enainsedemdeset let. Pod njim je bilo novejše: Marcus Bell, devetnajst let. Oba sta bila na stopnicah, ko je prišel dim.
Na Linden Row je s svoje stopnice prišla približno oseminšestdesetletna ženska z bralnimi očali na verižici, Illuminari pa položila v roke pločevinasto skodelico.

**Perpetua**  
Dober večer, Varuh.

To je rekla zraku nad Dovovo ramo, z glasom, kakršnega človek uporabi za velikega psa, ki ga ima rad in se ga boji. Dov je pokimal in odšel proti naslednji svetilki. Illuminara je obstala s čajem ženske, ki se o njej še ni odločila, in občutila majhno nezasluženo srečo, ki je ni preučevala.
Na stopnicah Številke 9 je sedemletna deklica z ostankom krede risala po pločniku.

**Nell**  
To je sedem ulic. To je gospod Dov, ponoči stoji tukaj. To je mamino okno. Sem gre ogenj.

**Illuminara**  
In kam greš ti, ko pride?

**Nell**  
Dol. Ampak na dnu naših stopnic ni več vrat. Nekdo jih je odnesel.

Dov se je ustavil tri stopnice stran. Pogledal je v stopnišče, v bledi pravokotnik na ometu, kjer je nekoč nekaj viselo, in mišica ob zadnjem delu njegove čeljusti se je enkrat premaknila. Ni rekel, da ni vedel.
Illuminara je sedla na stopnico ob kredi in prosila, naj ji pokaže mamino okno.

scenes.title: Česar niso hoteli povedati
paragraphs: *Kuhinja Perpetue Vane, Linden Row · pet dni pred napadom, 21:15*

Dov je odšel na rečne stopnice na nočno stražo. Kuhinja je dišala po čebuli in radiatorskem prahu. Prišla sta dva človeka in sedela v plaščih, kakor sedijo ljudje, ki bodo morda pozneje morali reči, da jih nikoli ni bilo tam.

**Teodor**  
Medicinske sestre za bratovo dializo ni bilo že devet dni. Reševalci ob črti prosijo za Varuhovo besedo, Varuh pa je na drugem koncu sedmih ulic. Ne povejte mu, da sem to rekel. Mojega fanta je potegnil iz reke.

**Perpetua**  
Zapišite po tem vrstnem redu. Radi ga imamo. Nato: že tri tedne nismo imeli obiskovalca, glasovanja ali poroke. In ko pride taktična enota, bo polovica od nas stala za njim, ker ni nikjer drugje stati.

**Illuminara**  
To bi mu rada prenesla. Samo tisto, kar mi dovolite prenesti.

**Teodor**  
Povejte mu o medicinski sestri.
Perpetua je šla do predalnika in se vrnila s škatlo za piškote. V njej je ležal debel sveženj rožnatih in rumenih indigo papirjev, zmehčanih od prijemanja.

**Perpetua**  
Devetnajst let sem razpošiljala za Marrow and Pike. Za vsak požar na stopnišču v Rise obstaja delovni nalog dva ali tri dni prej. Odstrani samozapiralna protipožarna vrata, zamenjaj z navadnimi. Odobril G. Pell. Kopije sem vzela v tej škatli tistega dne, ko so me odpustili, ker sem takšna ženska. Dvakrat sem jih odnesla na mestni svet. En najemnik s škatlo je pritožba. Rekli so mi, da nimam pravnega položaja.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj vam ga da?

**Perpetua**  
Registrirano telo. Sedem podpisov, po eden z vsake ulice, in predsedujoči. Potem mora inšpektor odpreti spis, in to je razlika med pritožbo in primerom. Imam šest ulic. Nimam ulice, ki sindikatu zaupa bolj kakor možu na črti.
Illuminara je obrnila kopije. G. Pell. G. Pell. Datum, stopnišče in tri dni pozneje požar. Prišla je razumet človeka, v rokah pa je držala knjigo evidenc, in videla je, da je to isto opravilo.

scenes.title: Streha Številke štiri
paragraphs: *Številka 4 Linden Row, streha · štiri dni pred napadom, 05:10*
Dov je sedel na parapetu s škornji nad ulico in gledal, kako se za rečnimi žerjavi dviga sivina. Stala je tri korake stran, dokler ni rekel, da sme bliže.

**Illuminara**  
Nekateri so mi povedali stvari, ki jih vam niso mogli. Dovolili so mi, da jih povem. Jih želite slišati?

**Dov**  
Povejte jih.

Povedala jih je v vrstnem redu, ki ga je zahtevala Perpetua. Radi ga imamo. Brez obiskovalcev, brez glasovanj, brez porok. Polovica nas stoji za vami, ker ni nikjer drugje stati. In medicinska sestra. Poslušal je, kakor je nekoč gotovo poslušal merilnik med spustom, ne da bi se premaknil.

**Dov**  
Teodor je to rekel.

**Illuminara**  
Zadnje.

**Dov**  
Sam sem jo zavrnil enajsti dan. Ne bi vam znal povedati zakaj. Nosila je telovnik.
Spodaj je po Linden Row peljal mlečni dostavnik. Nebo je začelo ločevati strehe.

**Dov**  
Hočete, da odstopim.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Če bi nocoj odstopili, bi bili človek s pokojnino in mrtvim stopniščem, Pell pa bi bil nazaj do polnoči. Zid ostane, dokler na njegovem mestu ne stoji nekaj drugega. Hočem vedeti, česa vas je strah na dan, ko vas ni tukaj.

**Dov**  
Da sem na rečnih stopnicah. Hanneina vrata, Marcusova vrata, obakrat sem bil na napačnem koncu okrožja. V vodi sem dober. Ogenj gre po stopnišču navzgor. En človek ne more biti na devetih stopniščih.

**Illuminara**  
Tudi jaz ne.
Perpetuine kopije je položila na parapet, fotografirane in poravnane. Prebral je prvo in nato naslednjo s potapljačevo potrpežljivostjo ter s palcem sledil vsaki vrstici kakor zapisu.

**Dov**  
Odobril G. Pell. Koliko jih je?

**Illuminara**  
Za zdaj enajst. Perpetua jih ima več. Same so pritožba. Potrebuje sedem ulic, ena od njih pa je vaša.

**Dov**  
In sindikatu ne zaupajo bolj kakor meni.

**Illuminara**  
Ne še. Mislim, da bi mu lahko, če bi vi sedeli v zadnji vrsti.

scenes.title: Sedem podpisov
paragraphs: *Dvorana na Linden Row · tri dni pred napadom, 19:30*

Štirideset zložljivih stolov, grelnik za čaj, igralna miza z blokom. Perpetua je sedela za blokom. Šest ulic je že podpisalo. Sedež rečne ulice je bil prazen, njen najverjetnejši predstavnik pa je slonel ob zadnji steni s prekrižanimi rokami, medtem ko so ga njeni prebivalci skrbno ne gledali.

**Perpetua**  
Sedite, Varuh. Sedeži so po ulicah.

Sedel je. Inšpektorica Amara Hale, ki je tisto popoldne prišla čez tlakovce z lastnim požarnovarnostnim nalogom, z Illuminarino roko nad razbitim tlakom in Dovom, ki se je ob črti umaknil, namesto da bi jo ustavil, je počakala, da so stoli nehali drsati.

**Hale**  
Dvorani bom povedala, kar sem povedala ob traku. Danes sem vstopila na lastno pristojnost, da si ogledam vaša stopnišča, on pa se je odločil, da me ne bo ustavil. To je bilo vse. Ne morem odpreti spisa o okrožju, katerega vrata drži en človek, in primera ne bom gradila na vratih, ki mi jih odpira en človek.

**Dov**  
Potem premaknem črto. Moja beseda pri tlakovcih za vas, gasilce in vsakega policista z nalogom. Ne za taktično enoto.

**Perpetua**  
Vaša beseda je težava, Varuh. Zelo dobra beseda je in beseda enega človeka.

**Hale**  
Dve stvari, in prosim, slišite ju ločeno. Nocoj, brez spisa in naloga, lahko po požarnem zakoniku namestim gasilsko vozilo in posadko znotraj vaše črte ter odredim vgradnjo samozapiralnih vrat na vsakem stopnišču, kjer manjkajo. To so nevarnosti, ki jih vidim. Primer je druga stvar. Kopije v škatli za piškote so vzorec, ne dokaz. Najprej jih povežem z evidenco sveta in izvajalčevimi računi, kar traja dva dni, nato pa spis, praviloma v dvainsedemdesetih urah. Če najdem človeka s kantom, ničesar od tega ne potrebujem. Pridržim ga. Poveljnica Ruiz pa vstopi triindvajsetega, če ji ne morem pokazati nečesa, kar deluje.

**Perpetua**  
Potem preberemo pogoje. Prvič. Sedem predstavnikov nadzoruje dostop ulic, vsak z enim glasom, z dvigom rok v tej dvorani. Drugič. Noben predstavnik, nobena ulica in noben Varuh ne zavrne medicinske sestre, obiskovalca, poroke ali gasilskega vozila. Tretjič. Straža odgovarja razporedu, razpored tej dvorani, vsakega predstavnika pa je mogoče odstaviti z dvigom rok.

**Teodor**  
Dvaindvajset dni ste držali tisto črto za nas in nikoli se vam nisem zahvalil, zato vas bom vprašal naravnost. En glas. Brez vrat. In če vas preglasujemo, to sprejmete in sedete.

**Dov**  
In naslednji, ki pride po Calder Lane s kantom?

**Perpetua**  
Sreča Teodorja in razpored.
Dov je dolgo gledal blok. Roke so se mu počasi razklenile, kakor da bi bilo treba vsako posebej prepričati.

**Dov**  
Potem najprej pas. Nocoj, preden ima eno samo stopnišče stražo. Gasilno vozilo, ki mora čakati pri mojih tlakovcih, ni zaščita, temveč usluga. Dvaindvajset dni sem držal tista vrata. En glas. Brez vrat. Da.
Perpetua je poklicala k dvigu rok rečno ulico in glasove preštela dvakrat, ker nihče v dvorani ni zaupal hitremu štetju.

**Perpetua**  
Enajst proti osem. Rečna ulica pošilja Dova Kessarina. Osem vas mu lahko pove zakaj, v obraz, v tej dvorani, kadar hočete.

Blok je zakrožil. Zapisanih je bilo sedem imen, po eno za ulico. Zadnje je bilo Dov Kessarin, Številka 4 Linden Row, predstavnik. Preden je podpisal, je list prebral do konca, kakor je moral pred vsakim potopom prebrati vsako dovoljenje.

**Perpetua**  
Straža na stopniščih. Dva na stopnišče, vsak z radijsko postajo, nihče sam na podestu. Teodor ima Devetico in obiskovalec gre z njim.

**Illuminara**  
Moja izmena, brez posebnega položaja.

**Perpetua**  
Vedro boste držali kakor tujec. Dobro. Naučili vas bomo.

Zunaj je Perpetua tisto popoldne v predvidevanju s kredo označila gasilski pas: tri metre širok, po vsej dolžini tlakovcev, z belimi črtami kakor prehod za pešce, ki ga je zarisal nekdo z zamero. Dov je stal pri prvem tlakovcu in pogledal nazaj proti vratom dvorane, kjer je štirideset ljudi prišlo gledat. Enkrat je spustil škorenj. Tlak se je vzdolž krede razmaknil kakor led na ribniku in se ustavil pri črtah.

Ko so prišle lopate, je sedel na robniku z velikimi dlanmi med koleni. Illuminara je odpeljala prvo samokolnico. Tehtala je toliko, kolikor tehta samokolnica. Do jutra je bil pas odprt in Haleino gasilsko vozilo je stalo znotraj črte z ugasnjeno modro lučjo, edina stvar v okrožju, ki bi lahko znova zaprla cesto, pa je bilo glasovanje.

scenes.title: Številka devet
paragraphs: *Številka 9 Calder Lane, stopnišče · dve noči pred napadom, 02:40*
Razpored je Dova postavil na rečne stopnice, šeststo metrov od Calder Lane. Sam je prosil za to. Bil je napačen konec okrožja in hotel je videti, kaj to stane.

Pri Številki 9 je stražil Teodor na podestu v pritličju, Illuminara pa dve nadstropji više s termovko in radijsko postajo, ki jo je držala kakor izposojen instrument. Dvajset do treh je vonj dosegel prej kakor zvok: bencin, nato dim, ki se je valil po odprtem grlu stopnišča, kjer bi morala biti spodnja vrata.

**Teodor**  
Devetica, Devetica. Moški ob vznožju s kantom. Ogenj je na stopnicah. Gasilci, Devetica. Drayevi so v tretjem.

To je izrekel s popolnoma mirnim glasom, glasom nočnega bolničarja. Illuminara je bila mimo drugega podesta, še preden je končal. Po ulici navzdol, v odprtini, ki pred dvema dnevoma ni obstajala, je zagnal motor.

Podest v tretjem nadstropju je zagorel. Plamen je pojedel navadna lesena vrata in se vzpenjal po nosilcih, Drayevih pet in babica na kuhinjskem stolu pa so stali na vrhu stopnišča, ki jih ne bi več preneslo. Plošča se je ugreznila in počila. Illuminara ji je podstavila hrbet. Nekoč je držala most; to je bilo lažje in gorelo je, pa si ni rekla, da je samo podest. Teža ji je šla prek ramen v steno. Družina je šla mimo nje v vrsti, babico je nesel najstarejši fant, skozi vročino, ki je dišala po njenih laseh.

Spodaj je straža počela tisto, čemur je straža namenjena. Teodor je skozi vrata usmeril gasilni aparat v vznožje ognja in ga podal sosedu iz prvega nadstropja, ki je vzel drugega s stene in stopil ob njega. Moški v odsevnem telovniku sveta, ki je poskušal steči proti pasu, se je znašel s ključavnico za kolo okoli gležnja in Teodorjem na sebi. Gasilno vozilo je v štiridesetih sekundah prišlo po pasu, skozi odprtino, ki si jo je okrožje izglasovalo, njegova posadka pa je do vrat razvila cev.

Na rečnih stopnicah, šeststo metrov stran, je neki moški odložil termovko in vse to poslušal po sprejemniku: Teodorjev glas, gasilsko vozilo, poveljnika posadke, ki je sporočal, da je tretje nadstropje prazno. Tekel je, še preden se je končalo.
Ko je Dov prišel po Calder Lane, je bilo stopnišče črno in mokro, Drayevi pa so bili pod odejo na pločniku.

**Dov**  
So vsi zunaj?

**Teodor**  
Vsi. To je Cole Rudd, Marrow and Pike, monter. Sedim na njem.

**Dov**  
To je bilo brez mene.

**Illuminara**  
Da.

**Teodor**  
Pas je sindikatov. Izglasovali smo ga. Bili ste tam.

**Dov**  
Ena stvar.
To je rekel tiho, kakor se odčita globina. Nato je sedel na robnik poleg moža v odsevnem telovniku, ki ga je gledal s posebnim strahom nekoga, ki je pričakoval zid, našel pa soseda.

scenes.title: Predstavnikov stol
paragraphs: *Zapora na Calder Lane · jutro napada, 05:00*

Hale je dva dni preživela v arhivu sveta s Perpetuino škatlo, lastno knjigo računov družbe Marrow and Pike in uradnikom, ki ji ni bil nič dolžan. Enajst kopij se je ujemalo z enajstimi računi, podpis G. Pell pa s podpisom na plačilnem seznamu. Rudd, ki so ga zadržali po požaru, je nehal govoriti, da se je izgubil.

Ob petih je sama vročila naloge s šestimi uniformiranimi policisti in predstavnikom vsake ulice ob njih. Pella so prijeli v stanovanju v pristaniškem okrožju; dispečerja, ki je tipkal naloge, pri zajtrkovalnem pultu, z delovno knjigo v plašču. Na vsakem stopnišču v Rise so vgradili protipožarna vrata ali objavili nalog za vgradnjo, pogodba družbe Marrow and Pike pa je bila zamrznjena do revizije. Lastniki so že najemali odvetnike, je suho rekla Hale, Rise pa bo še vedno imel svojo inšpektorico.
Taktična enota ni vstopila. Ruiz je stala ob traku z isto skodelico.

**Ruiz**  
Ukaz je prišel ob štirih. Uniformirani policisti z nalogi, v spremstvu vaših predstavnikov. Moji ostanejo pri zapori. Ne preklicujem ga, ker je primer končan. Ni. Preklicujem ga, ker moji enoti ni ostalo nič, česar že ne počnejo gasilski pas, razpored in nalog. Zapisati hočem, da še vedno mislim, da je zid zid.

**Dov**  
Je. Petindvajset dni sem bil zid. Zaradi tlaka bom izgubil dovoljenje.

**Ruiz**  
Obtoženi boste zaradi tlaka in opomnjeni za ostalo. Zapisala bom, da ste razbili štirideset metrov, ki vam jih je dalo glasovanje, in niti centimetra več.

**Dov**  
Zapišite, da je straža obdržala Številko 9. Mene ni bilo tam.

Tisto jutro nič ni vrnilo Hanne Ostrov ali Marcusa Bella. Illuminara, z dlanmi v belih obvezah, ki do večera ne bodo več potrebne, je njuni imeni enkrat izgovorila v mislih in nikomur ni ponudila nauka.

Dov je črto prečkal peš, po pasu, ki ga je razbil sam, in ni udaril z nogo. Perpetua je na drugi strani čakala s knjigo glasov, dvorana za njo pa se je polnila za prvo polno sejo sedmih predstavnikov. Medicinska sestra za dializo je prišla skozi pas prvo jutro po odprtju, v telovniku, in štiri ure sedela s Teodorjevim bratom. Zdaj je bila v četrti vrsti s termovko. Dovu ni rekla nič in on nič njej, nato pa je čez trenutek umaknila torbo s stola ob sebi.

**Perpetua**  
Sedež po ulicah, predstavnik. Četrta vrsta. Sedeli boste ob medicinski sestri.

Sedel je. Knjigo glasov je odprl na prvi prazni strani in z rokopisom moža, ki je vso kariero zapisoval globine, napisal vrstico: Številka 9, spodnja vrata, vgraditi danes. Straža nocoj: Teodor, Dray, Kessarin.

Zunaj dvorane je Nell na novo risala svoj zemljevid. Človeka, ki je ponoči stal, na njem ni bilo več. Namesto njega je narisala sedem majhnih krogov, po enega za ulico, v sredini pa večjega s streho in vrati ter z velikimi črkami, visokimi kakor ona: DVORANA.

Illuminara je sedela na robniku med krednim prahom z uničenimi dlanmi v naročju in poslušala okrožje, kako ustvarja zvok, ki ga petindvajset dni ni bilo, zvok štiri tisoč ljudi, ki se prepirajo o stolih.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara ne poruši zidu Dova Kessarina; posluša, dokler sedem ulic zidu ne more nadomestiti z izglasovanim gasilskim pasom, skupno stražo in zamenljivim predstavnikom, Dov pa se svobodno odloči, da bo sedel med ljudmi, ki jih je varoval.

late_publication.reason: Published later, on 18 November 2026, by BD's decision. The GPT scheduled tasks were out of usage on 17 November, so the 21:00 day freeze was never created and the nightly publisher could not run. The stories were completed and closed on 17 November; Claude also reviewed and closed S2 and S3 as a recorded stand-in for GPT. The original Claude reader files were unusable (a storage-format error), so both reader scores were made afterwards, after the 20:30 cutoff, by fresh isolated readers (GPT in a ChatGPT chat, Claude in a sandboxed one-shot call); the Slovenian translations of S2 and S3 were made later in ChatGPT chats.
late_publication.reason_sl: Objavljeno naknadno, 18. novembra 2026, po BD-jevi odločitvi. GPT-naloge 17. novembra zaradi omejitve porabe niso tekle, zato zamrznitev dneva ob 21:00 ni nastala in nočni objavljalnik ni mogel teči. Zgodbe so bile dokončane in zaključene 17. novembra; Claude je zgodbi S2 in S3 tudi pregledal in zaključil kot zapisano nadomestilo za GPT. Prvotne Claudove bralske datoteke so bile neuporabne (napaka v obliki zapisa), zato sta obe bralski oceni nastali pozneje, po rezu ob 20:30, pri svežih izoliranih bralcih (GPT v klepetu ChatGPT, Claude v peščenem enkratnem klicu); slovenska prevoda zgodb S2 in S3 sta nastala pozneje v klepetih ChatGPT.
